guide.summary: Each customer authorizes the registered app through Dropbox OAuth 2 for an individual account, and the resulting user token is used to list entries. The permission boundary is the files.metadata.read scope on an App Folder-scoped app, which covers metadata reads only.
guide.recommendation: Each customer authorizes the registered app through Dropbox OAuth 2 for an individual account, and the resulting user token is used to list entries. The permission boundary is the files.metadata.read scope on an App Folder-scoped app, which covers metadata reads only.

findings.title: Individual customer OAuth user token
findings.detail: Apps requesting only User API scopes receive a token associated with the user who authorizes the app. Each customer signs into dropbox.com and grants the app access to their data, then the app uses the returned token as a Bearer token.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects their own individual Dropbox account; no team administration.

evidence.quote: Apps that request only scopes from the User API will receive a token associated with the user that authorizes the app.
Overview When working with the Dropbox APIs, your app will access Dropbox on behalf of your users. You’ll need to have each user of your app sign into dropbox.com to
user on the Dropbox app authorization page where the user consents to sharing their data.

findings.title: Register the app and configure redirects before first test
findings.detail: The app must be registered in the Developer Console to obtain an app key and secret, and exact redirect URIs must be added under the OAuth 2 section of Settings. Dropbox checks the redirect_uri at authorization time.
findings.appliesWhen: Before any customer authorization or listing test.

evidence.quote: Before you can get started, you’ll need to register your app with Dropbox by creating a new app in the Developer Console
. That page will guide you through the process of registering your app, selecting permissions, and obtaining an app key and secret (a.k.a. client_id and client_secret ) and inputting redirect
You’ll need to register the exact redirect URI(s) your app may use in the Developer Console

findings.title: Select App Folder file access when creating the app
findings.detail: Content access must be set to App Folder, so the app acts only on data within its app folder (in the /apps folder) and not the full Dropbox.
findings.appliesWhen: When creating the app in the Developer Console for this request.

evidence.quote: App Folder: Your application will be able to take actions allowed by its scopes on data within its app folder only (in the /apps folder). This option is suitable for
your Dropbox application, you will also be prompted to select the scope of file access. Currently, these two options are:
apps that export content or manage only their content.

findings.title: files.metadata.read scope for listing names
findings.detail: This is the required scope for list_folder and list_folder/continue. It permits reading file and folder metadata, which covers names; it does not grant content download, upload, edit, move or delete. Within the App Folder setting, it applies only to the app folder.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer authorization and every list_folder or list_folder/continue call.

evidence.quote: Required scope: files.metadata.read Endpoint format: RPC
list_folder . Required scope: files.metadata.read
OR Authorization Bearer OAuth 2.0 token issued to a specific user. Use Authorization: Bearer <token> .

findings.title: Request minimal scopes to avoid review and acceptance impact
findings.detail: Dropbox advises asking only for the least permissions required, because requesting more scope may result in users not accepting the OAuth request and could impact app review.
findings.appliesWhen: Before launch, when selecting scopes in the Permissions tab.

evidence.quote: Minimal Access Always ask for the least amount permissions required by your applications. Requesting more scope and content access than required may result in end users not accepting your OAuth
request and could impact your app review process.
When using API scopes, you may also ask for minimal permissions at authorization time - then re-authorize at later time if and when your application requires more permissions from the

steps.title: Register the Dropbox app with Scoped access and App Folder file access
steps.detail: In the Dropbox Developer Console, create a Scoped access app with App Folder access, enable only files.metadata.read on the Permissions tab, save changes, and add the exact redirect URI under Redirect URIs in the OAuth 2 section of Settings. Note the app key (client_id) and app secret (client_secret). Do not enable team scopes or full Dropbox access.
steps.doneWhen: The app is registered with App Folder access, only files.metadata.read enabled, a redirect URI configured, and client_id and client_secret recorded.

evidence.quote: Choose Scoped access as the API type.
App folder : Access limited to a single folder in the user’s Dropbox.

steps.doneWhen: The customer approves the request and the browser is redirected to the registered redirect_uri with an authorization code.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Call the token endpoint with the authorization code returned by the consent callback, grant_type=authorization_code, the redirect_uri used in authorization, and client credentials. This is an unexecuted authorization step; it must be run only after the customer consent step completes. The returned access_token is used as the Bearer token for listing.
steps.doneWhen: The token response contains an access_token and expires_in, and the token is stored for the listing test.

evidence.quote: Call the /oauth2/token endpoint with your app’s client_secret to exchange the code for an access token in order to make API calls
Your application exchanges the authorization code for an access token that can be used to make secure calls to the Dropbox API (not shown)
In your request to the /oauth2/token endpoint, pass the code_verifier with your generated value instead of the client_id .

fields: code: authorization code from the callback
grant_type: authorization_code
redirect_uri: same value used during authorization
client_id and client_secret: from app registration

steps.title: List the first page of App Folder entries
steps.detail: Call list_folder with path set to the empty string to list the root of the App Folder, using the customer's access token. Set recursive to false. Read entries[].name for file and folder names and check has_more and cursor. Expected success: HTTP 200 with entries, cursor and has_more. Boundary check: request a documented non-existent or excluded path is not sufficient; instead confirm no content endpoint is called and that a files.content.read request is not issued.
steps.doneWhen: The response returns HTTP 200 with an entries array, a cursor, and a has_more boolean.

evidence.quote: Starts returning the contents of a folder. If the result’s ListFolderResult.has_more
Response Successful response cursor string >=1 character
--data ' {"path": ""} '

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: from the authorization exchange
path: empty string for App Folder root
recursive: false
entries[].name: name of each file or folder
cursor and has_more: pagination state from response

steps.title: Continue listing with the returned cursor until has_more is false
steps.detail: While the previous response has has_more set to true, call list_folder/continue with the cursor from the prior response. Collect entries[].name from each page. Stop when has_more is false. Preserve the same access token. Documented end condition: has_more is false.
steps.doneWhen: All pages are retrieved and the final response returns has_more false.

steps.title: Continue App Folder listing with the cursor from the first page
steps.detail: Use the cursor returned by list_folder when has_more is true to call list_folder/continue. Repeat with each new cursor until has_more is false. This is the continuation for the first request; prose alone does not satisfy pagination.
